notes.gdp: GDP is Eurostat's quarterly national accounts, seasonally and calendar adjusted. Figures before Croatia joined the euro in 2023 are converted from kuna at the fixed rate of 7.53450 kuna per euro.
notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets; the Croatian Bureau of Statistics headlines its national CPI, which can differ by a few tenths. Croatia joined the euro on 1 January 2023 and has had no policy rate of its own since: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate, from that date. Before 2023 the Croatian National Bank ran its own policy, which is not shown.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). Croatian news often quotes the employment service's registered unemployment rate instead, a different measure. Employment and participation rates are Eurostat's seasonally adjusted Labour Force Survey figures for ages 15 to 64, from 2009; the unadjusted series go back to 2002 but swing several points each year with the tourist season.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Croatia imports far more goods than it exports, a gap largely covered by tourism, which is a service and so not shown here.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is Eurostat's monthly long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (the EU's benchmark Croatian government yield), which runs about a month behind; the exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page.
